title.en: The Works of Heaven and the Inception of Things: Author’s Preface

edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource; the signature line is printed without its parentheses.
edition.zh: 据维基文库；署名一行去掉括号。

basis.en: Late Ming text printed in 1637; the author died about 1666.
basis.zh: 明末文本，1637 年刊行，作者约卒于 1666 年。

note.en: Song Yingxing’s preface to his illustrated account of crafts and production, printed in 1637 with a friend’s help. He apologises for being too poor to buy samples or gather colleagues, writes for princes who have never seen a plough, and ends by telling ambitious scholars to toss the book aside because it will not help them in any examination. Notice the order of the book: grain first, gold and jade last.
note.zh: 宋应星为他那部图文并茂的工艺之书写的序，1637 年在友人资助下刊行。他抱歉自己贫穷，无力购物考证、招集同人；他为没见过耒耜的王孙写作；最后请功名之士把这书弃掷案头，因为它与功名进取毫不相关。留意全书的次序：五谷在前，金玉在后。

excerpt.orig: 丐大業文人，棄擲案頭，此書于功名進取毫不相關也。
excerpt.en: Let the ambitious men of letters toss it aside on their desks: this book has nothing whatever to do with advancement in examinations and office.
excerpt.zh: 丐大业文人，弃掷案头，此书于功名进取毫不相关也。
